_metadata.title: Selection, Installation and Maintenance of First-Aid Fire Extinguishers — Portable and Mobile — Code of Practice (Fifth Revision)
_metadata.description: Structured fire extinguisher rules for the FireRuleX rule engine. All rules are sourced directly from IS 2190:2024.

fireClasses.description: Classification of fire types per IS 2190:2024 clause 3.4

classes.A: Fires involving solid combustible materials (wood, paper, rubber, plastics). Cooling effect needed.
classes.B: Fires involving flammable liquids or liquefiable solids. Blanketing effect needed.
classes.C: Fires involving flammable gases under pressure. Inhibition needed.
classes.D: Fires involving combustible metals (magnesium, aluminium, zinc, sodium, potassium). Special media needed.
classes.F: Fires involving cooking media (vegetable or animal oils/fats). Also called kitchen fire.

hazardClassification.description: Hazard type classification based on building characteristics

low.label: Low (Light) Hazard
low.description: Minor quantity of Class A combustibles. Offices, classrooms, churches, assembly halls, hotel guest rooms.

moderate.label: Ordinary (Moderate) Hazard
moderate.description: Greater amounts of Class A combustibles and Class B flammables. Dining areas, mercantile shops, light manufacturing, auto showrooms, workshops.

buildingHeightM.note: Not applicable as a standalone criterion

high.label: High Hazard
high.description: Large amounts of Class A combustibles and Class B flammables. Woodworking, vehicle repair, aircraft servicing, cooking areas, painting, dipping, coating.

extinguisherTypes.description: Types of portable fire extinguishers and their applicable fire classes

foam_afff.label: Foam (AFFF/FFFP) Type
foam_afff.note: Not for water-soluble flammable/combustible liquids unless specifically rated

dcp_abc.label: Dry Chemical Powder (ABC Type)
dcp_abc.note: Residue may damage delicate electronic equipment

co2.label: Carbon Dioxide (CO2) Type
co2.note: Metal horns not safe for energized electrical equipment. Suitable for clean environments (no residue).

clean_agent.label: Clean Agent Type
clean_agent.note: Use where clean medium is required (server rooms, archives). Regulated by Montreal Protocol.

generalPrinciples.description: Overarching principles that apply across all fire classes (IS 2190:2024, clause 7.1)

rules.rule: The selection of fire extinguishers for a given situation shall be determined by the character of the fires anticipated, the construction and occupancy of the property, and the vehicle and contents to be protected.
Required fire extinguishers shall be provided on each floor level of a building.
All buildings with combustible construction or combustible contents require a minimum complement of Class A fire extinguishers.
Hazards of different classes (B, C, D, F) that are present in a building require extinguishers specific to the hazard class IN ADDITION to the Class A complement.
Where different hazard types exist on the same floor, the most stringent criteria shall apply for extinguisher placement.
Class B/C/D/F extinguishers shall NOT be used as substitutes for Class A extinguishers. They are supplementary.

classA.description: Placement requirements for Class A fire extinguishers (solid combustibles — wood, paper, rubber, plastics)

generalRules.rule: At least 2 extinguishers per floor level. Exception: floors with area < 100 m² may have 1 extinguisher.
Higher-rated extinguishers may be used provided max travel distance and max floor area per unit are not exceeded.

moderate.note: Two 2A water-type extinguishers installed adjacent may substitute one 3A.

high.note: Two 2A water-type extinguishers installed adjacent may substitute one 4A.

classBandC.description: Placement requirements for Class B (flammable liquids shallow depth ≤6mm) and Class C (flammable gas) hazards

generalRules.rule: At least 2 extinguishers per floor level. Exception: floors with area < 100 m² may have 1 extinguisher.
Two or more extinguishers of lower rating shall NOT be combined to meet Table 2 requirement. Exception: up to 3 AFFF-type extinguishers may be combined if sum of ratings meets minimum.
Buildings with Class B/C hazards must also have a standard complement of Class A extinguishers. Class B/C extinguishers are additional.

classBDeepFlammable.description: For flammable liquid hazards of appreciable depth (>6mm) — dip tanks, quench tanks

generalRules.rule: At least 144 numerical units of Class B extinguishing potential per m² of maximum fire area.
AFFF extinguishers may use 89B protection per m² of hazard (instead of 144B).
Travel distance to extinguishers shall not exceed 15 m.

classD.description: Combustible metal hazards (magnesium, aluminium, zinc, sodium, potassium)

generalRules.rule: Class D extinguishers shall be provided for hazards involving combustible metals.
Travel distance shall not exceed 20 m.
Size and number shall be determined by specific combustible metal, physical particle size, and area. Consult fire professional.

classF.description: Class F: cooking media fires (vegetable or animal oils/fats) in cooking appliances

generalRules.rule: Class F extinguishers shall be provided for any cooking appliance area.
Travel distance shall not exceed 10 m.
Size and number based on total cooking area per Table 3.
Electrical hazards are themselves Class A or Class B — size on that basis.
Must use extinguishers suitable for energized electrical equipment: CO2, ABC powder, clean agent, or water-mist types.
generalRules.note: CO2 with metal horns NOT safe for energized electrical equipment.

rules.rule: Extinguishers shall be fully charged, operable, and kept in designated places at all times.
Extinguishers shall be conspicuously located along normal paths of travel, including exits.
Cabinets housing extinguishers shall not be locked, unless vandalism risk exists — in that case, emergency access means are required.
Extinguishers shall not be obstructed or obscured from view. Location signs required where visual obstruction cannot be avoided.
Extinguishers shall be installed on hangers, brackets, or in cabinets. Floor stands allowed where wall mounting is not possible.
Portable extinguishers (≤17 kg) — top of extinguisher shall not be more than 1.5 m above floor. Clearance from floor shall not be less than 30 mm.
Operating instructions shall face outwards or toward the most likely direction of access.
Extinguishers shall not be installed in areas where temperatures are outside the range marked on the extinguisher.
Extinguisher must be checked when initially placed in service and approximately every 90 days thereafter.

checks: Unobstructed and visible, operating instructions facing outward
Seals and tamper indicators not broken or missing
Not damaged, corroded, or leaking; nozzle not clogged
Inspection tag, ID number, and HPT tag intact
Exterior cleaned and returned to designated place

maintenance.frequency: Annually (once a year, not less than 6 months apart)

rules.rule: All extinguishers must be maintained at least once a year (not less than 6 months apart), at time of hydrostatic testing, and when indicated by inspection.
Extinguishers out of service for maintenance or recharge shall be replaced immediately by spare extinguishers of same type and at least equal classification/rating.

extinguisherLifetime.note: Lifetime measured from date of manufacture. Extinguisher failing hydrostatic pressure test must be discarded immediately.

obsoleteExtinguishers.description: These types MUST be removed from service immediately
types: Non-rechargeable types more than 5 years old
Copper or brass shell types joined by soft solder or rivets; steel shell types joined by rivets

commercialBuildingRules.description: Derived rules specifically for commercial buildings (MVP scope). Commercial buildings typically fall under Moderate hazard with Class A fire potential and possibly Class B (flammable storage/goods).

hazardDetermination.method: Use Table 6 (Annex B) criteria: building height, occupant count, floor area, flammable material quantities
hazardDetermination.commercialDefault: Moderate hazard unless criteria indicate Low or High

mandatoryChecks.rule: All commercial buildings with combustible construction or contents require Class A extinguishers
At least 2 Class A extinguishers per floor level. If floor area < 100 m², 1 is acceptable.
Number of Class A extinguishers = ceiling(floorArea / maxAreaPerExtinguisher). Use Table 1 values by hazard type.

mandatoryChecks.check: Class B extinguishers if flammable liquids present
mandatoryChecks.rule: If flammable liquids are present (e.g., generator room, paint storage, kitchen fuel), additional Class B extinguishers needed per Table 2. PLUS standard Class A complement is still required.
Where energized electrical equipment is present (UPS rooms, server rooms, electrical panels), CO2, ABC powder, clean agent, or water-mist extinguishers required.
Any cooking area with vegetable/animal oil appliances requires Class F extinguisher. Travel distance ≤ 10 m. Sized by cooking area per Table 3.
Minimum ratings per hazard type — Low: 2A/55B, Moderate: 3A/144B, High: 4A/233B
